{
  "problem_addressed": "Searching for signatures of the QCD critical point by studying non-monotonic variations in high-order moments of net-proton number fluctuations in Au-Au collisions.",
  "methodology": "Measurements of net-proton cumulant ratios using the STAR detector at RHIC over a broad range of collision energies. Corrections for finite impact parameter range, track reconstruction efficiencies, and volume fluctuations were applied to the data.",
  "experiments": "Data collected from Au-Au collisions ranging from \u221aN\u2082N = 7.7 to 200 GeV. Analysis focused on central (top 5%) and peripheral (70-80%) collisions.",
  "results": "Observed a statistically significant (3.1 sigma) non-monotonic variation in kappa-sigma squared (\u03ba\u03c3\ufe0f) vs collision energy in central Au-Au collisions, indicative of proximity to the QCD critical point. No such variation was detected in peripheral collisions or baseline models without a critical point.",
  "limitations": "Systematic uncertainties could affect interpretation but were accounted for in analyses. Critical point prediction suggests existence at higher baryon chemical potentials than explored in this study.",
  "future_work": "Higher event statistics would enable differential measurements and improved comparisons with QCD calculations, aiding confirmation of the critical point hypothesis.",
  "main_contributions": [
    "First evidence of non-monotonic variation in \u03ba\u03c3\ufe0f as a function of collision energy for central Au-Au collisions with significance relative to Skellam expectation.",
    "Demonstration that baseline models without a critical point cannot explain the observed non-monotonic behavior."
  ],
